# Joby Aviation to Acquire Resonant Sciences for $500M as Defense Business Expands

FCW Team

By

FCW Team

August 11, 2026 at 9:54 AM EDT

Listen 10:53

FuelCellsWorks

Joby Aviation to acquire defense leader Resonant Sciences, creating a scaled defense growth platform. (Credit: Joby Aviation & Resonant Sciences)

Electric air-taxi developer will add around 250 aerospace specialists and technologies spanning sensing, communications and aircraft systems while establishing Resonant as its dedicated defense division

Acquisition will significantly expand Joby’s defense business by adding a fast-growing company with established programs, classified capabilities and scaled manufacturing operations.

...

(NYSE: JOBY) today announced that it has entered into a definitive agreement to acquire Resonant Sciences, a Dayton, Ohio-based defense technology company, for approximately $500 million.

The acquisition will represent a significant expansion of Joby’s defense business, delivering immediate scale through a rapidly growing and EBITDA-positive business supporting active U.S. national security programs.

Resonant also brings classified infrastructure, qualified products, established production operations and longstanding customer relationships, as well as a deeply experienced technical team. By bringing together the companies’ complementary aerospace engineering capabilities, the combination will create a scaled defense growth platform that accelerates autonomy and expands the applications for Joby’s technology.

**Joby’s Dedicated Defense Business Unit**
Upon closing, Resonant will become Joby’s dedicated defense business and continue to operate under the Resonant Sciences name, led by Co-Founder and CEO J. Micah North. Joby’s existing defense initiatives, which are built on more than a decade of work with defense and intelligence customers, will be consolidated within the new business unit. These include the development of dual-use turbine-electric and hydrogen-electric aircraft, as well as a dual-use autonomy technology stack. Housing this work within Resonant will allow Joby’s commercial aviation organization to maintain its primary focus on certifying, manufacturing, and commercializing its electric air taxi.

The combination of Joby and Resonant is also expected to create significant opportunities in adjacent markets.

...

Resonant supports sensitive and critical defense programs via its long-standing Facility Security Clearance (FCL) and accredited facilities, with more than 90 percent of its team members holding security clearances, providing the cleared technical workforce and infrastructure required to execute sensitive programs at scale.

Beyond developing RF hardware, Resonant performs end-to-end payload integration and aircraft modification. Its electronics, apertures and radomes are qualified across more than 20 commercial and defense airframes.

The capabilities of the two companies are highly applicable to the defense sector’s next generation platforms, which reflect a broader shift in defense priorities toward autonomous, lower-cost aircraft, for which advanced sensing, electronic countermeasures and resilient communications are central to mission effectiveness.

That gives Joby something it does not have to build from scratch: an established defence engineering and manufacturing operation with national security customers, specialised technology and personnel working on programmes that can already move through the defence procurement system.

The deal is more than an expansion into another market. It shows how quickly the business plans of the leading US electric vertical take-off and landing (eVTOL) companies are changing. Joby and rival Archer Aviation are still pursuing air taxis, but both are now putting greater weight on military and government applications that can reach customers sooner.

## Joby Aviation expands defence business as FAA air taxi certification advances

The acquisition comes at an important point for Joby’s commercial programme.

...

## Archer Aviation’s Boeing deal highlights growing defence focus among eVTOL manufacturers

Archer has been pursuing the same basic idea from a different direction.

Earlier this week, [Archer agreed to acquire Boeing’s Wisk Aero](https://aerospaceglobalnews.com/news/archer-wisk-insitu-skygrid-boeing-deal/) , drone maker Insitu and airspace-services company SkyGrid in an all-stock transaction. Boeing would receive shares representing 19.75% of Archer’s Class A stock and gain the right to appoint a director to Archer’s board.

Wisk_Shot_03-1920x1080 Photo: Wisk Aero

The deal gives Archer access to Wisk’s autonomous-flight technology, while Insitu brings an established defence business into the company.

Insitu generates more than $200 million in annual revenue and is already profitable, according to a Reuters report. That is significant for a company whose core air-taxi business has yet to generate substantial revenue.

...

“From raw performance to producibility, harnessing the best technologies from the commercial eVTOL market for defense is central to how Thunder will deliver operational value to our customers,” he said.

Archer’s commercial aircraft, [Midnight](https://aerospaceglobalnews.com/tag/archer-midnight/) , remains central to the company’s plans. But the company is now developing a parallel route in which its experience with electric propulsion, vertical flight and autonomous systems can be applied to military aircraft.

Archer-Midnight-1024x823 Photo: Archer Aviation

That is an important change in the economics of the sector.

Instead of waiting for millions of passengers to begin using air taxis, the companies can pursue government and defence customers for aircraft, autonomous systems, sensors and other technologies that can generate revenue earlier.

## Resonant Sciences gives Joby’s Aviation an established US defence technology platform

Joby’s approach is more concentrated.
Rather than acquiring several businesses, it is taking control of one established defence technology company and making it the foundation of a dedicated defence division.

Resonant has already expanded its manufacturing capacity and nearly doubled its highly skilled technical workforce since Cerberus invested in the company in 2023. Cerberus said Resonant has also moved technologies from research and development into production-ready offerings and expanded its customer and programme base.

Cerberus Senior Managing Director and Co-Head of Supply Chain Michael Palmer said the investment had focused on building the operational base needed to scale.

“Over the past three years, we expanded manufacturing capacity, advanced key technologies into production, and deepened relationships with customers,” Palmer said.

Resonant CEO J. Micah North said the company had retained its focus on national security customers while expanding its ability to execute more programmes.

...

## Military contracts could generate revenue ahead of large-scale air taxi operations

There is no indication that Joby is abandoning its passenger aircraft. Its latest financial results show the company continuing to push through the final phase of FAA certification, increase aircraft production and prepare for passenger operations.

But the Resonant acquisition changes the scale of its ambitions.

Joby will have a defence organisation with its own engineering, manufacturing and national security capabilities. It can pursue defence aircraft and mission systems while its commercial aircraft moves through the final stages of certification and towards passenger operations.

The combination of Joby and Resonant is also expected to create significant opportunities in adjacent markets.
An early focus is expected to be the integration of Joby’s dual-use autonomy stack with Resonant’s Radio Frequency sensing and signal-processing capabilities, accelerating the development of software-defined autonomous systems for defense customers.

JoeBen Bevirt, Founder and CEO of Joby Aviation said: “The combination will pair Resonant’s established capabilities with Joby’s globally leading aircraft propulsion technologies, creating a powerful platform for the next phase of Resonant’s growth.”

Joby’s existing defence initiatives, which are built on more than a decade of work with defence and intelligence customers, will be consolidated within the new business unit. These include the development of dual-use turbine-electric and hydrogen-electric aircraft, as well as a dual-use autonomy technology stack.

# Joby Aviation to acquire Resonant Sciences in $500 million defense deal

[By Clement Charpentreau](https://www.aerotime.aero/articles/author/clement-charpentreau "View all posts by Clement Charpentreau")

Edited By [Emma Yates-Badley](https://www.aerotime.aero/articles/author/emmayatesbadley "Emma Yates-Badley")

August 11, 2026

[Defense](https://www.aerotime.aero/category/defense "Defense") A Joby Aviation electric vertical takeoff and landing aircraft following a ground test at Edwards Air Force Base California A Joby Aviation electric vertical takeoff and landing aircraft following a ground test at Edwards Air Force Base, California, on September 20, 2023. (Credit: US Air Force photo)

Joby Aviation announced on August 11, 2026, that it has entered into a definitive agreement to acquire Resonant Sciences, a Dayton, Ohio-based defense technology company, for approximately $500 million.
The deal gives the California eVTOL developer immediate scale in the defense sector through an already profitable business supporting active US national security programs.

Founded in 2015, Resonant designs, manufactures and delivers radio frequency (RF) and mission systems for US national security customers and is a global leader in low-observability technologies, structures and subsystems. The roughly 250-person company also works in advanced sensing, electronic countermeasures, communications and autonomous systems.

## A profitable defense business

Resonant generated more than $100 million in trailing-12-month revenue, up approximately 40% year over year, with adjusted EBITDA margins in the high teens. Bookings in the first half of 2026 were more than three times higher than in the same period of 2025, and backlog more than doubled year over year.

...

aero/articles/joby-ohio-manufacturing-facility) , the acquisition will give the companies close to one million square feet of manufacturing, integration and testing space in the Dayton region.

JoeBen Bevirt, founder and CEO of Joby Aviation, described the deal as pairing “Resonant’s established capabilities with Joby’s globally leading aircraft propulsion technologies.” North said joining Joby gives his team “additional engineering depth, aircraft platforms, autonomy technology and production expertise.”

Joby plans to fund the acquisition with approximately $450 million in cash and $50 million in Joby common stock, with certain Resonant employee stockholders retaining an ongoing equity stake. The transaction is expected to close in the first half of 2027, subject to regulatory approval.

## Joby and Archer go defense shopping

The announcement comes a day after Joby’s closest rival made an almost identical move.
Archer Aviation [agreed to acquire Boeing’s Wisk Aero, Insitu and SkyGrid subsidiaries](https://www.aerotime.aero/articles/archer-acquire-boeing-wisk-insitu-skygrid) on August 10, 2026, a deal built around Insitu, the profitable ScanEagle and Integrator drone maker that generates more than $200 million in annual revenue.

Within 24 hours, both leading eVTOL developers had moved to buy their way into established, revenue-generating defense businesses rather than wait for their own military programs to mature.

com%2Fnews%2Fjoby-aviation-to-scale-defense-business-through-acquisition-of-resonant-sciences&text=Joby%20Aviation%20to%20Scale%20Defense%20Business%20Through%20Acquisition%20of%20Resonant%20Sciences)

**SANTA CRUZ, Calif. and DAYTON, Ohio — August 11, 2026 —** Joby Aviation, Inc. (NYSE: JOBY) today announced that it has entered into a definitive agreement to acquire Resonant Sciences, a Dayton, Ohio-based defense technology company, for approximately $500 million. The acquisition will represent a significant expansion of Joby’s defense business, delivering immediate scale through a rapidly growing and EBITDA-positive business supporting active U.S. national security programs.

  
Resonant also brings classified infrastructure, qualified products, established production operations and longstanding customer relationships, as well as a deeply experienced technical team.
By bringing together the companies’ complementary aerospace engineering capabilities, the combination will create a scaled defense growth platform that accelerates autonomy and expands the applications for Joby’s technology.

  
  
**Joby’s Dedicated Defense Business Unit**

  
Upon closing, Resonant will become Joby’s dedicated defense business and continue to operate under the Resonant Sciences name, led by Co-Founder and CEO J. Micah North.

  
Joby’s existing defense initiatives, which are built on more than a decade of work with defense and intelligence customers, will be consolidated within the new business unit. These include the development of dual-use turbine-electric and hydrogen-electric aircraft, as well as a dual-use autonomy technology stack. Housing this work within Resonant will allow Joby’s commercial aviation organization to maintain its primary focus on certifying, manufacturing, and commercializing its electric air taxi.

...

Resonant supports sensitive and critical defense programs via its long-standing Facility Security Clearance (FCL) and accredited facilities, with more than 90 percent of its team members holding security clearances, providing the cleared technical workforce and infrastructure required to execute sensitive programs at scale.

  
Beyond developing RF hardware, Resonant performs end-to-end payload integration and aircraft modification. Its electronics, apertures and radomes are qualified across more than 20 commercial and defense airframes.

  
The capabilities of the two companies are highly applicable to the defense sector’s next generation platforms, which reflect a broader shift in defense priorities toward autonomous, lower-cost aircraft, for which advanced sensing, electronic countermeasures and resilient communications are central to mission effectiveness.

Joby Aviation, Inc. (NYSE: JOBY) today announced that it has entered into a definitive agreement to acquire Resonant Sciences, a Dayton, Ohio-based defense technology company, for approximately $500 million.
The acquisition will represent a significant expansion of Joby’s defense business, delivering immediate scale through a rapidly growing and EBITDA-positive business supporting active U.S. national security programs.

These include the development of dual-use turbine-electric and hydrogen-electric aircraft, as well as a dual-use autonomy technology stack. Housing this work within Resonant will allow Joby’s commercial aviation organization to maintain its primary focus on certifying, manufacturing, and commercializing its electric air taxi.
